Tony de Zorzi

A Johannesburg batsman who captained his country's under-19s, made Test hundreds and belonged to the side that won the 2025 World Test Championship final.

Where it began

Tony de Zorzi's story starts in Johannesburg, where he was born on 28 August 1997. He went to King Edward VII School in the city and later studied at the University of Pretoria, a fair sign that he could plan a long innings off the field as well as on it.

He was marked out early. In 2016 South Africa made him captain of their squad for the Under-19 World Cup, and that same year he made his senior debut for Northerns, first in T20 cricket against Kenya and then in first-class and one-day cricket.

The player

Runs followed at every level. He made his first one-day hundred for Titans against Knights in January 2018, and was soon trusted to lead the Cricket South Africa Emerging Squad. In January 2020 he made his first double hundred, an unbeaten 213 against Cape Cobras, and later moved to Western Province.

His Test debut came against the West Indies in February 2023. Later that year he made an unbeaten 119 against India at St George's Park on a pitch that made batting hard work, and South Africa won to square the one-day series. In October 2024 he made his first Test hundred, against Bangladesh. In 17 Tests from 2023 to 2025 he scored 919 runs at 30.63, with two hundreds, three fifties and a best of 177, and held 13 catches.

What made him special

De Zorzi's game had a touch of the captain about it. He was asked to lead at under-19 level, again with the Emerging Squad and once more when South Africa A toured Sri Lanka in 2023. Selectors do not hand out that job to players who panic.

He could dig in when conditions were hard, as that hundred at St George's Park showed. If his Test average does not quite match the size of his best scores, it simply means he saves the big ones for when they count. A man who has made 177 in a Test and 213 not out in a first-class match plainly enjoys staying in.

Away from the middle

He was part of the squad that won the World Test Championship final in 2025, a proud line on any cricketer's record. He also played franchise cricket for Tshwane Spartans in the Mzansi Super League.

And finally

Early in his career he was named in the Pretoria Mavericks squad for a new T20 league, which was postponed and then cancelled before a ball was bowled. It must be the only team he ever joined without facing a ball, and none of that was his fault.
